title: Case 001: Recipient cannot attend the scheduled delivery window

details.data: Entirely synthetic; English; fictional geography; all times UTC

context: A desk-lamp parcel is at the destination depot. The recipient cannot use the original slot. Dispatch, not the desk, controls booking changes.
initial_request: I have a work meeting during the morning delivery. Could you help move my lamp delivery? Please use this order-linked message thread.
overview: The escalation snapshot comprises history events 001–002. Event 003 records the next agent action; the subsequent events provide the disclosed calibration follow-through. Facts learned later must not be used as if already known at escalation.

next_action.summary: Ask the recipient to choose from dispatcher-confirmed alternative slots.

outcome: Dispatch confirms the selected replacement slot; delivery itself remains pending.
boundaries: Do not promise arrival at a precise minute or say the lamp has been delivered.

events.body: DL-001 is booked for 2026-02-03, 09:00–12:00 UTC. Our rescheduling inventory currently has 2026-02-03 15:00–18:00 or 2026-02-04 10:00–13:00. There is no rescheduling charge.
I have a work meeting during the morning delivery. Could you help move my lamp delivery? Please use this order-linked message thread.
Dispatch has offered 2026-02-03 15:00–18:00 or 2026-02-04 10:00–13:00, both at no charge. Which should I ask them to book?
Please choose 2026-02-03 15:00–18:00. I will be home then.
Following your booking request with Vessa’s selection, DL-001 is now reserved for 2026-02-03 15:00–18:00. The morning slot has been removed. This is a booking confirmation, not a completed delivery.
